questions.question: Define current and potential difference with their formulas and units, and explain the through/across distinction that decides how each is measured.
questions.expected_answer: Current is the rate of flow of charge, I = Q/Δt, in amperes (1 A = 1 C/s); it flows THROUGH a component, so an ammeter is connected in series with very low resistance. Potential difference is the work done per unit charge, V = W/Q, in volts (1 V = 1 J/C); it exists ACROSS two points, so a voltmeter is connected in parallel with very high resistance. Conventional current is drawn from the positive terminal through the circuit to the negative terminal.

questions.question: Distinguish emf from terminal potential difference, state which is larger when current flows, and tell the energy story of why a battery goes flat.
questions.expected_answer: The emf is the voltage across the battery's terminals when no current flows (open circuit); the terminal pd is the voltage across the terminals when current flows, and it is slightly lower because the battery spends some energy internally. In the battery, chemical potential energy is converted to electrical energy carried by the charge; in resistors it is converted to heat and light. The charge circulates unconsumed — the battery goes flat when its chemical energy is used up, not its charge.

questions.question: Give the microscopic description of resistance and use it to explain the effect of length, thickness and temperature on a wire's resistance.
questions.expected_answer: Drifting electrons collide with the vibrating positive ions of the metal lattice, transferring kinetic energy that appears as heat — this opposition is resistance (unit: ohm, 1 Ω = 1 V/A). A longer wire means more lattice to cross and more collisions, so higher resistance; a thicker wire gives more parallel room for the drift, so lower resistance; a hotter wire has more violently vibrating ions and more frequent collisions, so higher resistance. Material matters too: copper conducts easily, nichrome resists strongly and is used in heating elements.
